dispositionRule: No pair has a disposition other than UNCLASSIFIED (to be decided by the oracle) or EXCLUDED-PRE-REGISTERED in this registration, and every pair has included=false. Dispositions are assigned only after this registration merges to main, by running the registered oracle command against the merge commit.

denominator.pairingRule: A pair is a .calr file and the .cs file with the same directory and stem. manifest.json names exactly these pairs: benchmarks (per-pair metric loop), bugScenarios (buggy variants), and editTasks (edited variants). Every .calr and every hand-written .cs under the corpus root at the cutoff belongs to exactly one pair; every other file is listed in corpus-inventory.json as non-pair with a reason.

locations.role: the corpus the static calculators read
contract scope exclusion; 7 .calr files and no C# arm at the cutoff, so 0 pairs

denominator.pairIdRule: pairId is the corpus-relative path of the pair without extension (for example DomainProblems/CsvParser). manifest ids are not unique at the cutoff (050 to 059 each name two pairs), so they are recorded per pair but never used as identifiers.

taskStatement.definition: The task statement of a pair is the manifest.json entry that names it at the cutoff, rendered as 'key: value' lines (source, id, name, category, level, features, notes; or the scenario id, description, category, and the pair it is a variant of). taskStatementSha256 is the SHA-256 of that UTF-8 text.
taskStatement.limitation: These are the only task statements that exist at the cutoff. Both arms of a pair are registered against the same statement, but it specifies no inputs, outputs, or failure behavior. The contract defines equivalence relationally (same inputs, same outputs, same failures) and requires an executed differential check as evidence, which the oracle provides. The oracle does not check either arm against the statement: two arms that are wrong in the same way are EQUIVALENT to each other, and no result may claim that a pair implements its statement.
taskStatement.interpretation: The contract's equivalenceDefinition says both sides 'implement the same task statement'. This registration reads that relationally: both arms are registered against one shared statement, and the executed differential check establishes that they compute the same observable function. It does not establish that either arm satisfies the statement, because the cutoff statements specify no outputs. If the maintainer reads the clause as requiring conformance to the statement, EQUIVALENT additionally needs per-pair task assertions registered by an amendment before the oracle runs (or a #1407 amendment); until then no pair may be reported as conforming to its statement.

oracle.command: dotnet run --project tests/Calor.Evaluation -c Release -- pair-oracle --registration docs/plans/evidence/b1-1276/registration --registration-commit <full SHA of the main commit that merged this registration> --output <file outside the repository, run 1>; then the same command with --compare-with <run 1 file> --output <file outside the repository, run 2>
oracle.runAgreement: The first run exits 4: it is not a result. The second run (--compare-with the first) reconciles them. It is invalid unless the first run has the same oracleId, oracleVersion, inputGeneratorVersion, registrationCommit, pairsSha256, and environment and exactly the same pair ids. A pair whose verdict differs between the runs is UNCLASSIFIED (NONDETERMINISTIC_ACROSS_RUNS). The second file keeps its raw verdicts (runResults) and the reconciled ones (results) and exits 0 only when valid, otherwise 3. Both files are retained; there is no rerun-until-agreement.
oracle.isolation: Each pair runs in its own child process (300,000 ms limit). A crash is UNCLASSIFIED (ORACLE_CRASH); exceeding the limit is UNCLASSIFIED (TIMEOUT).
steps: 1 identity: the SHA-256 of both files must equal the registered calorSha256 and csharpSha256; otherwise UNCLASSIFIED (IDENTITY_MISMATCH) and nothing runs.

2 build: the Calor arm is compiled to C# by Calor.Compiler.Program.Compile with default CompilationOptions (the compiler's default contract mode). Then each arm's C# is compiled by the same Roslyn compilation: LanguageVersion.Latest, library output, Release, nullable enabled, deterministic, the Microsoft.NET.Sdk implicit global usings, and one reference set (the oracle process's trusted platform assemblies). An error in either arm is NOT-EQUIVALENT (BUILD_FAILED_CALOR, BUILD_FAILED_CSHARP, or BUILD_FAILED_BOTH).

3 surface: each arm's surface is the public static methods of its exported static classes, keyed by lower-cased name, exact parameter types, and exact return type, without the declaring type. A static Main() or Main(string[]) is one C# entry-point member keyed by its return type alone and run once, with an empty argument array where it takes one. Types the arm defines itself key as arm-defined. Any other exported type (class, struct, record, interface, enum, delegate: these can carry constructor, override, or inherited behavior) and any other public member of a static class (field, property, event) is unsupported; accessors and the type initializer are not separate members (a type initializer runs on the first call and its failure is observed). A duplicated key in one arm is NOT-EQUIVALENT (SURFACE_AMBIGUOUS); a key in only one arm is NOT-EQUIVALENT (SURFACE_MISMATCH); otherwise anything unsupported is UNCLASSIFIED (UNSUPPORTED_SURFACE); no key at all is UNCLASSIFIED (SURFACE_EMPTY); any key whose parameter or return type the input generator does not support is UNCLASSIFIED (UNSUPPORTED_TYPE).
4 inputs: for every key, in ordinal key order, the registered input generator produces the input tuples (see inputs). Both arms receive the same tuples in the same order.

5 execution: each tuple is invoked twice per arm in the order Calor, C#, Calor, C#, each time with fresh copies of array and list arguments, stdout captured, stdin empty, a fresh empty working directory, invariant culture, a 16 MB thread stack, and a 2,000 ms limit. An observation is: return, throw (the call threw), or throw-while-reading-result (the call returned but enumerating or rendering the result threw), the canonical return value, the exception's full type name, stdout, the arguments after the call, and the name and SHA-256 of every file created in the working directory. Any invocation over the limit makes the pair UNCLASSIFIED (TIMEOUT). An arm whose two observations of one tuple differ makes the pair UNCLASSIFIED (NONDETERMINISTIC).

6 decision: if any field of any tuple's Calor observation differs from its C# observation, NOT-EQUIVALENT (OBSERVATION_MISMATCH), with up to 5 witnesses. Otherwise EQUIVALENT (AGREE). Every result records the surface, the number of tuples, and observationsSha256, the SHA-256 of the full observation transcript.

inputs.supportedTypes: bool, char, byte, short, int, long, uint, ulong, float, double, decimal, string; Nullable<T> of those; one-dimensional arrays and List<T>, IList<T>, IReadOnlyList<T>, IEnumerable<T>, ICollection<T>, IReadOnlyCollection<T> of those (passed as T[] or List<T>). Return types: the same, or void.
inputs.boundaryValues: The fixed pools in InputGenerator.Pools (for example int: 0, 1, -1, 2, -2, 3, 5, 7, 10, 15, 100, -100, 1000, int.MaxValue, int.MinValue; string includes null and the empty string; double includes -0.0, NaN, and both infinities). Collections: null, empty, one element, three elements, four elements with a repeat, and the whole pool.
inputs.tuples: If the product of the parameters' pool sizes is at most 256, the full cartesian product; otherwise one diagonal tuple per index of the longest pool, parameter j taking pool[(i + j) mod length]. Then 64 seeded random tuples. A member with no parameters gets one empty tuple.
inputs.seed: SplitMix64 seeded with the first 8 bytes (big-endian) of SHA-256('b1-1276-signature-inputs-v1|' + pairId + '|' + memberKey). The seed depends only on the pair id and the member key, never on either arm's code or output.
inputs.goldenValues: None. No input or output was computed by running either arm before registration.

expectedOutputs.definition: For every registered input, the expected observation of each arm is the other arm's observation: the same kind (return or throw), the same canonical return value (InputGenerator.Render: culture-invariant, round-trip floating point, exact strings, element-wise collections), the same exception type, the same stdout, the same argument state after the call, and the same created files.
expectedOutputs.limitation: An EQUIVALENT disposition means no disagreement on this finite input set. It is not a proof of equivalence on all inputs.

failureBehavior.rule: On every input both arms return, or both throw an exception of the same full type name. A build failure in either arm is NOT-EQUIVALENT. A timeout or crash is UNCLASSIFIED. No pair registers a different failure behavior, and no exception type is normalized to another.
failureBehavior.consequence: A Calor contract failure (a Calor.Runtime exception type) and a C# ArgumentException on the same input are different failures, so such a pair is NOT-EQUIVALENT. The rule applies identically to both arms.

fairness: Every step except the Calor-to-C# compilation treats both arms identically: same Roslyn version and options, same references, same global usings, same inputs in the same order, same timeouts, same stack, same culture, same comparison.
Inputs depend only on the pair id, the member key, and the parameter types. Neither arm's code or output influences them.
The oracle never reads a metric value. A disposition cannot depend on which arm is shorter.
The exact-type failure rule and the case-insensitive member-name match apply in both directions; no exception type is normalized.
Every tuple is invoked in the same interleaved order (Calor, C#, Calor, C#), and observations are compared only after all four are recorded.

controls.synthetic: tests/Calor.Evaluation/Tests/PairDifferentialOracleTests.cs: synthetic pairs written for the test, none of them registered. Positive controls must be EQUIVALENT; each negative control differs in one observable respect (one boundary output, return vs throw, exception type, stdout, argument mutation, a created file, a CsvParser-shaped surface, an unsupported property, a non-static class, a result that fails only when enumerated, a build error, changed bytes, nondeterminism, a hang) and must get its specific reason. Reconciliation (provenance, pair-id set, cross-run changes, known witness) is tested on synthetic verdicts, and the preflight's commit checks on this checkout.

knownWitness.source: contract.json benchmarkEquivalence and section 5 name this pair as the known non-equivalence witness (#1276).
knownWitness.rule: The reconciling second run checks this pair. If it is not NOT-EQUIVALENT, the result is invalid (valid=false, nonzero exit): no disposition from it is used, and the oracle needs an amendment before another run.

limitations: v1 drives static methods of static classes only. Pairs with any other exported type or public member, or with types the arm defines itself, are UNCLASSIFIED, not EQUIVALENT.
Equivalence is checked on a finite input set and is not a proof.

Effects other than return values, exceptions, stdout, argument state, and files created under the working directory (absolute paths, network, environment, static state between tuples) are not observed.
oracle.preflight: Before any pair runs, in both the parent and the per-pair child mode, the command refuses (exit 2) unless HEAD equals --registration-commit, the checkout is clean (no edited tracked file and no untracked, non-ignored file anywhere, so no unregistered source can enter the build), every file in sha256.json matches its seal, and every oracle implementation file matches its pinned hash. Outputs are written outside the repository. The output records the .NET runtime, OS, architecture, and Roslyn version.

metrics.summary: One comparative metric (TokenEconomics CompositeTokenEconomics, a symmetric source-size ratio). Seven static metrics whose per-arm scores use language-specific rules are descriptive only.

statistics.population: The comparative population is the set of registered pairs with source manifest.benchmarks that the oracle dispositions EQUIVALENT. The corpus is fixed and author-constructed. It was not sampled from any population of programs, tasks, or developers, so no result generalizes beyond these files.
statistics.perPairValue: ln r, where r is the pair's CompositeTokenEconomics AdvantageRatio from the pinned TokenEconomicsCalculator.
statistics.pointEstimate: Geometric mean of r over included pairs: exp(mean of ln r). Overall estimate weights every included pair equally; per-category estimates use the pairs of that manifest category.

interval.algorithm: Order the included pairs by ordinal pairId (within the category for a per-category interval); n is their count. Seed one SplitMix64 generator (the InputGenerator.SplitMix64 algorithm) with state 1276 per interval. For b = 1..10000, draw n indices, each NextUInt64() mod n, and compute the geometric mean of r over the drawn pairs (exp of the mean of ln r, in double precision, summed in draw order). Sort the 10000 values ascending; the interval is [value at 1-based rank 250, value at 1-based rank 9750].
interval.stratification: the overall interval resamples all included pairs; a per-category interval resamples within that category
interval.label: corpus-resampling interval for this fixed corpus; not a confidence interval for any population

alsoReported: pairs per disposition and per exclusion
count of included pairs with r > 1, r < 1, and r = 1
statistics.runRule: The static metric run is executed twice on the same commit. Every per-pair value must be bit-identical between the runs; any difference means no result is produced. The two runs are a determinism check, not two samples.
removed: metrics.*.ci95 computed from a single category aggregate (zero-width interval)
intervals, standard deviations, Cohen's d, and paired t-tests over repeated deterministic runs
an overall advantage defined as the geometric mean of category geometric means
any ranking or win count that treats a descriptive-only metric as comparative
headlineConditions: every registered pair has a disposition from a valid reconciled oracle result (known-witness control passed)
no included pair has a disposition other than EQUIVALENT
the result's dispositioned pair manifest names this registration's pairManifestSha256 as its registration and keeps every registered pair, path, and hash
the result's comparability key equals this registration's key in every field except pairManifestSha256, which is the SHA-256 of that dispositioned manifest

comparability.aggregationMethod: b1-1276-agg-v1: geometric mean of r over EQUIVALENT program pairs; percentile bootstrap over pairs, 10000 resamples, SplitMix64 seed 1276, 95%; no interval below 2 pairs

comparabilityNote: pairManifestSha256 here is the hash of the registration pair manifest. A result's pairManifestSha256 is the hash of its own dispositioned manifest, which must name this registration's hash; results with different dispositioned manifests are not comparable. No earlier benchmark result is comparable with a result of this method. generatorVersion names the results generator that the second #1276 PR implements exactly as statistics.interval.algorithm specifies.
afterRegistration: Any change to a pinned field (a pair's files or hashes, task statement, input set, expected outputs, failure behavior, the oracle and its command or implementation files, the metric set or implementation files, the aggregation and interval method, the sampling unit, or an exclusion) is a #1407 amendment. BenchmarkRegistrationTests fails when any packet file, the document, a corpus file, an oracle file, or a metric implementation file differs from this registration, and it pins the SHA-256 of sha256.json as a constant, so a regenerated and resealed packet still fails until that constant is changed in a reviewed amendment.
A pair repaired, dropped, or re-dispositioned after registration stays reported with its previous disposition.
Historical benchmark artifacts (website/public/data/benchmark-results.json and its derivatives) stay historical; they are not regenerated in place or relabeled as outputs of this method.
claimRule: Static feature scores are not coding-agent outcomes. Neither is presented as a measured language, productivity, correctness, or safety advantage.
